description: types.rs:35-48 — 'impl TryFrom<jmap_chat_types::Presence> for ContactPresenceFilter' has 'type Error = ()'. Unit-typed errors are an anti-pattern: callers using '.try_into()?' have to absorb the unit into their own error type and have no way to surface what went wrong. The actual failure case is precise and meaningful: 'Presence::Other(s) cannot be used as a filter value' — the wire string the server sent should be preserved for diagnostics. Idiomatic fixes: (a) 'type Error = jmap_chat_types::Presence' — returns the input on failure so the caller can inspect it; (b) a typed 'pub enum PresenceFilterError { OtherNotFilterable(String) }' that carries the wire string; (c) at minimum 'type Error = &'static str' with a descriptive constant. Engineering basis: error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields lose values the caller might want — the unit form loses even the type info, which is strictly worse.
title: TryFrom<Presence> for ContactPresenceFilter uses 'type Error = ()' — loses context
